voice.text: A river can wind across a flat valley. Each bend changes where the water cuts into the bank and where it leaves sediment behind.
Look at the channel from above. The water follows curves, but the banks are also changing as the river flows.
On the outside of a bend, faster water can erode the bank. On the inside, slower water often drops sand and gravel.
Over time those two changes can move the bend sideways. A winding river is always reshaping its path.
